text: Creatine supplementation increases intramuscular creatine and can improve repeated high-intensity exercise performance and training adaptation. The position stand reports creatine monohydrate as the most studied form and describes recommended use as generally well tolerated in healthy people.

metadata.source_title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation in exercise, sport, and medicine

text: Recommended creatine doses are commonly 3 to 5 grams per day or about 0.1 gram per kilogram per day. Water retention can occur, especially early in supplementation, but creatine does not increase fat mass and a loading phase is not required. Body-mass changes alone cannot identify whether a person's facial fullness is edema or fat.

metadata.source_title: Common questions and misconceptions about creatine supplementation: what does the scientific evidence really show?

text: A meta-analysis of 49 resistance-training trials found small additional gains in strength and fat-free mass from protein supplementation. Its breakpoint analysis found no further average fat-free-mass gain above a total protein intake near 1.62 grams per kilogram per day; this is a population estimate, not a universal individual threshold.

metadata.source_title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults

text: For most healthy exercising adults, total daily protein around 1.4 to 2.0 grams per kilogram is generally sufficient. Per-meal needs vary with body size, age, training, and protein quality; the position stand gives a general range of 0.25 gram per kilogram or 20 to 40 grams of high-quality protein per serving and emphasizes total daily intake over a narrow post-workout window.

metadata.source_title: International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise

text: No single hydration measure is sufficient in all settings because body water shifts among compartments and each method has limitations. Body mass, urine measures, thirst, and bioimpedance should be interpreted together and under standardized conditions; a short-term scale change or one home sign cannot by itself confirm edema or dehydration.

metadata.source_title: Reviewing the current methods of assessing hydration in athletes

text: Hydration assessment methods include changes in body mass, blood and urine measures, bioelectrical impedance, and clinical observations. There is no single gold standard; repeated measurements are more interpretable when timing, food and fluid intake, exercise, and measurement conditions are kept consistent.

metadata.source_title: Assessing hydration status

text: Exercise can reduce total fat mass and improve body composition and metabolic health even when scale weight changes little. Fat distribution and visible definition vary across people, and a body-fat percentage does not map to a universal appearance threshold. Local appearance cannot be inferred from a single whole-body estimate.

metadata.source_title: Effect of Exercise Training on Fat Loss-Energetic Perspectives and the Role of Improved Adipose Tissue Function and Body Fat Distribution

text: A systematic review of wrist activity trackers found acceptable performance for some step-count and heart-rate measurements, but energy-expenditure error exceeded 30 percent across all tested brands. Calorie-burn estimates should therefore be treated as rough trend data rather than precise numbers for food replacement or energy-balance calculations.

metadata.source_title: Accuracy and Acceptability of Wrist-Wearable Activity-Tracking Devices: Systematic Review of the Literature

text: A systematic review in screen users under 40 associated longer screen exposure and poor ergonomics with more digital-eye-strain symptoms. Evidence did not support blue-blocking filters as prevention. Lighting, glare, viewing setup, breaks, blinking, refractive correction, and persistent symptoms should be considered without assuming one cause.

metadata.source_title: Digital eye strain in young screen users: A systematic review

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 45 randomized trials found no high-certainty evidence supporting the evaluated treatments for computer vision syndrome. Blue-blocking spectacles did not reduce visual-fatigue symptoms in the included trials; persistent pain, vision change, marked redness, or unilateral symptoms need clinical assessment rather than reliance on screen accessories.

metadata.source_title: Interventions for the Management of Computer Vision Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

text: Vitamin D toxicity is uncommon but can cause severe hypercalcemia, usually after excessive long-term supplement use or in conditions that alter vitamin D metabolism. Symptoms can include vomiting, abdominal pain, excessive thirst and urination, dehydration, confusion, and apathy. Dose, duration, other supplements, medications, kidney function, calcium, and measured 25-hydroxyvitamin D affect risk.

metadata.source_title: Vitamin D Toxicity-A Clinical Perspective

text: Athletes commonly experience short or fragmented sleep, and sleep needs differ among individuals and across training, travel, competition, stress, and illness. The expert consensus recommends individualized assessment rather than treating one sleep-duration number as optimal for everyone; persistent impairment warrants evaluation of causes and schedule constraints.

metadata.source_title: Sleep and the athlete: narrative review and 2021 expert consensus recommendations

text: A systematic review found that 20 to 40 grams of casein before sleep can increase overnight protein synthesis in studied healthy adults, but long-term body-composition evidence is limited and group protein intakes were not always matched. Pre-sleep protein is optional and should be considered within total daily protein and individual tolerance.

metadata.source_title: Effects of pre-sleep protein consumption on muscle-related outcomes - A systematic review

text: A meta-analysis found no clear advantage of post-exercise stretching over passive recovery for strength recovery or delayed-onset muscle soreness at 24 to 72 hours. The evidence was sparse, heterogeneous, and very low certainty, so stretching may be used for preference or mobility goals but should not be promised to accelerate recovery.

metadata.source_title: The Effectiveness of Post-exercise Stretching in Short-Term and Delayed Recovery of Strength, Range of Motion and Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

text: Bioelectrical impedance estimates depend on device technology, equations, population, hydration, recent food and fluid, exercise, and measurement procedure. Consumer BIA is best used for standardized repeated trends rather than treating one body-fat percentage as exact or as a universal predictor of visible abdominal definition.

metadata.source_title: Assessment of Body Composition in Athletes: A Narrative Review of Available Methods with Special Reference to Quantitative and Qualitative Bioimpedance Analysis

text: A clinical series of recurrent orofacial swelling found a broad differential diagnosis, including inflammatory skin disorders, contact dermatitis, granulomatous disease, Crohn disease, sarcoidosis, and lymphedema. Appearance, brief pressure, or a cold compress is not a validated home test that reliably distinguishes edema from facial fat; time course, associated symptoms, exposures, examination, and sometimes testing are needed.

metadata.source_title: A Diagnostic Approach to Recurrent Orofacial Swelling: A Retrospective Study of 104 Patients

text: The clinical practice guideline for suspected rotator-cuff tendinopathy covers assessment, nonsurgical care, rehabilitation, prognosis, and return to work or sport. Shoulder pain during pressing should be managed from symptom behavior, function, load, examination findings, and red flags; one movement location alone does not establish a diagnosis.

metadata.source_title: Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy Diagnosis, Nonsurgical Medical Care, and Rehabilitation: A Clinical Practice Guideline

text: The 2021 multisociety chest-pain guideline uses structured risk assessment and diagnostic pathways rather than symptom reassurance alone. New chest pressure or pain with exertion, especially with shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, fainting, or radiation to the arm, jaw, back, or shoulder, requires prompt urgent evaluation; a conversational assistant cannot rule out a serious cause.

metadata.source_title: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 randomized trials found small benefits of creatine monohydrate for memory, attention time, and processing speed in adults. Certainty was moderate for memory and low for several other cognitive outcomes, so cognitive benefit should not be presented as established for every person or use case.

metadata.source_title: The effects of creatine supplementation on cognitive function in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of trials lasting at least six weeks found that creatine combined with resistance training produced a small average additional increase in directly imaged muscle thickness. The result supports a modest training adjunct effect, not a dramatic or guaranteed increase in regional muscle size.

metadata.source_title: The Effects of Creatine Supplementation Combined with Resistance Training on Regional Measures of Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of creatine trials found no evidence of renal damage at the studied doses and durations. This does not replace individualized clinical assessment for people with kidney disease, relevant medications, abnormal tests, or symptoms.

metadata.source_title: Effects of Creatine Supplementation on Renal Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

text: A narrative systematic review in combat-sport athletes found that creatine commonly increased body mass, fat-free mass, maximal strength, and power, while effects on sport-specific endurance, recovery, and fatigue were not demonstrated. The weight-class context matters because extra body mass can be a practical tradeoff.

metadata.source_title: Creatine Supplementation in Combat Sport Athletes: A Narrative Systematic Review

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 74 randomized trials found that increasing daily protein during resistance training produced small additional lean-mass and lower-body-strength gains in healthy adults. Intake targets are population findings and should not be treated as a precise individual requirement.

metadata.source_title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of protein intake to support muscle mass and function in healthy adults

text: In older adults with sarcopenia, a systematic review found small average advantages from whey protein plus resistance exercise for skeletal muscle mass and handgrip strength. Evidence quality was low to very low and this population-specific result should not be generalized directly to younger healthy lifters.

metadata.source_title: Effectiveness of Whey Protein Supplementation during Resistance Exercise Training on Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength in Older People with Sarcopenia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

text: A network meta-analysis of resistance-training trials found that several protein types and timings were associated with muscle or strength gains, but physical-performance outcomes did not show a significant benefit. Total diet, training, and adherence remain more important than treating a narrow timing window as mandatory.

metadata.source_title: Effects of Timing and Types of Protein Supplementation on Improving Muscle Mass, Strength, and Physical Performance in Adults Undergoing Resistance Training: A Network Meta-Analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials in young healthy adults found small-to-medium average effects of whey protein on restoration of muscle function within 24 to 96 hours after strenuous resistance training. The evidence base was limited, so whey should not be promised as a complete recovery solution.

metadata.source_title: The Effect of Whey Protein Supplementation on the Temporal Recovery of Muscle Function Following Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

text: A systematic review found that body-composition estimates from BIA depend on choosing equations appropriate to the device and the person's age, sex, health status, physical activity, and population characteristics. A device output is therefore an estimate tied to its method, not a direct measurement of body fat.

metadata.source_title: High-standard predictive equations for estimating body composition using bioelectrical impedance analysis: a systematic review

text: A systematic review in athletes found that BIA fat-mass estimates were inconsistent versus reference methods, while athlete-specific foot-to-hand equations showed better agreement for fat-free mass and body-water measures. Generalized equations can introduce systematic error, so repeat conditions and device consistency matter.

metadata.source_title: Bioelectrical impedance analysis versus reference methods in the assessment of body composition in athletes

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated agreement between DXA and BIA for athlete body composition. It reinforces that methods are not automatically interchangeable, so a consumer BIA percentage should not be translated into an exact DXA-equivalent value or a visual-appearance threshold.

metadata.source_title: Agreement Between Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry and Bioelectric Impedance Analysis for Assessing Body Composition in Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

text: A systematic review of bioelectrical impedance vector analysis in sport describes BIVA as a method influenced by body-water and tissue properties, with interpretation requiring population and measurement context. It does not justify diagnosing hydration, edema, or body-fat distribution from an isolated home-device reading.

metadata.source_title: Bioelectrical impedance vector analysis (BIVA) in sport and exercise: Systematic review and future perspectives

text: A sports-hydration review emphasizes matching fluid and electrolyte plans to the athlete, environment, exercise duration, sweat losses, and tolerance. Hydration guidance should be individualized rather than inferred from one scale change, a facial appearance change, or a single BIA reading.

metadata.source_title: Practical Hydration Solutions for Sports

text: The American College of Sports Medicine position stand on exercise and fluid replacement recommends an individualized approach based on exercise conditions and avoiding excessive dehydration or overdrinking. It is performance guidance, not a method for diagnosing medical swelling.

metadata.source_title: American College of Sports Medicine position stand. Exercise and fluid replacement

text: A review of athlete sweat-rate and sweat-sodium measurement found meaningful variability across and within people. A single estimated sweat profile should therefore be treated as a starting point to test and adjust, not a fixed prescription.

metadata.source_title: Sweating Rate and Sweat Sodium Concentration in Athletes: A Review of Methodology and Intra/Interindividual Variability

text: A collegiate-athlete sleep consensus describes sleep as relevant to health, well-being, and performance, while recognizing schedule, travel, academic, and training constraints. Sleep advice should account for the person's actual pattern and persistent impairment rather than impose one universal ideal.

metadata.source_title: Wake up call for collegiate athlete sleep: narrative review and consensus recommendations from the NCAA Interassociation Task Force on Sleep and Wellness

text: A systematic and meta-analytic review found acute sleep loss can impair aspects of physical performance, with effects varying by task and sleep-loss condition. It supports protecting sleep around demanding training or competition, without proving that one poor night determines an individual's result.

metadata.source_title: Effects of Acute Sleep Loss on Physical Performance: A Systematic and Meta-Analytical Review

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis found time-of-day variation in maximum endurance and strength performance, with substantial individual and protocol variation. When comparing training performance, repeated tests should be done under comparable timing and conditions.

metadata.source_title: Diurnal Variation in Maximum Endurance and Maximum Strength Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

text: A TFOS evidence review describes the digital environment as one contributor to ocular-surface symptoms through factors such as reduced blinking, visual demand, ergonomics, and environment. Screen discomfort is multifactorial and persistent or concerning eye symptoms need appropriate clinical assessment.

metadata.source_title: TFOS Lifestyle: Impact of the digital environment on the ocular surface

text: A Cochrane review found no reliable evidence that blue-light filtering spectacle lenses improve visual performance or prevent eyestrain in adults. They should not be presented as a proven remedy for screen-related discomfort.

metadata.source_title: Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults

text: A systematic review of commercial wearables found that validity and reliability differ by metric and device. Step and heart-rate estimates can be useful in some contexts, whereas energy-expenditure estimates require particular caution and should not be used as exact calorie accounting.

metadata.source_title: Reliability and Validity of Commercially Available Wearable Devices for Measuring Steps, Energy Expenditure, and Heart Rate: Systematic Review

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that consumer wearable activity trackers can increase physical-activity participation. A tracker may help behavior and monitoring, but its calorie estimate remains a device-derived approximation rather than a measured energy balance.

metadata.source_title: Consumer-Based Wearable Activity Trackers Increase Physical Activity Participation: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of Apple Watch health metrics found accuracy varies by measurement and study context. Consumer wearables can support trends, but they are not a substitute for clinical assessment or laboratory-grade energy-expenditure measurement.

metadata.source_title: Apple watch accuracy in monitoring health metrics: a systematic review and meta-analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis compared post-exercise recovery techniques and found that massage, compression, immersion, and cold exposure can reduce some soreness or fatigue measures, while effects differ by outcome and method. These tools are optional adjuncts rather than replacements for load management, sleep, nutrition, and time.

metadata.source_title: An Evidence-Based Approach for Choosing Post-exercise Recovery Techniques to Reduce Markers of Muscle Damage, Soreness, Fatigue, and Inflammation: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found that both heat and cold interventions can reduce delayed-onset muscle-soreness pain, particularly in the first day after exercise. It did not establish a universal best method or prove faster restoration of training capacity.

metadata.source_title: Heat and cold therapy reduce pain in patients with delayed onset muscle soreness: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 randomized controlled trials

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis found pressotherapy produced a modest reduction in muscle soreness after exercise but did not significantly improve jump performance or creatine-kinase outcomes. It should be considered an optional comfort intervention, not a primary recovery treatment.

metadata.source_title: The Effect of Pressotherapy on Performance and Recovery in the Management of Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

text: A network meta-analysis of exercise-induced muscle-damage studies compared cold-water immersion, contrast water therapy, thermoneutral or hot immersion, and cryotherapy. Results differed by outcome, so ranking a method for soreness or a biomarker does not make it a universal recovery solution.

metadata.source_title: The effects of hydrotherapy and cryotherapy on recovery from acute post-exercise induced muscle damage-a network meta-analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis reported that BCAA supplementation was associated with lower delayed-onset muscle-soreness ratings at several post-exercise time points, while biomarker effects varied by timing and outcome. This is not evidence that BCAAs are required for recovery or that they replace adequate dietary protein.

metadata.source_title: Attenuating Muscle Damage Biomarkers and Muscle Soreness After an Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage with Branched-Chain Amino Acid (BCAA) Supplementation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Meta-regression

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of rotator-cuff-related shoulder pain found motor-control exercise programs were probably slightly better than nonspecific exercise for disability, while several prescription details remained uncertain. Shoulder exercise should be progressed according to symptoms and function rather than self-diagnosed from one painful lift.

metadata.source_title: The Efficacy of Exercise Therapy for Rotator Cuff-Related Shoulder Pain According to the FITT Principle: A Systematic Review With Meta-analyses

text: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized trials found that supervised aerobic exercise was associated with modest reductions in weight, waist circumference, and body-fat measures in adults with overweight or obesity. Effects rose with exercise duration on average, but individual body-composition changes still vary.

metadata.source_title: Aerobic Exercise and Weight Loss in Adults: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy adults found aerobic and concurrent training reduced absolute fat mass more than resistance training alone in longer interventions, while body-fat-percentage differences between modes were not significant. Program duration and total workload matter more than a single universal exercise mode.

metadata.source_title: Comparison of concurrent, resistance, or aerobic training on body fat loss: a systematic review and meta-analysis

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis in young and middle-aged adults found both HIIT and moderate-intensity continuous training improved body-composition and fitness outcomes on average. Differences depended on population and program design, so HIIT is not a guaranteed superior fat-loss method for every person.

metadata.source_title: Effect of High-Intensity Interval Training vs. Moderate-Intensity Continuous Training on Fat Loss and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in the Young and Middle-Aged a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
